title: Weekly Markets Monitor - Waller the Dollar
gist: The World Gold Council's weekly monitor argues the US dollar's breakout above key technical resistance (BBDXY 1,229/1,233), driven by hawkish Fed talk including Governor Waller floating a 50bp December hike and a hot 0.4% m/m CPI, combined with ~30bp higher 10-year TIPS yields in November, forms a potential 'double whammy' headwind for gold.

insights.claim: The Bloomberg Dollar Spot Index broke a cluster of key technical resistance at 1,229/1,233 in mid-November 2026; a sustained hold above it would suggest a large USD base has formed and the core trend has turned higher.
insights.speaker: World Gold Council
insights.so_what: Watch 1,229/1,233 as the pivot: holding above favours long-USD and is bearish for USD-priced commodities.
insights.quote: A sustained hold above here would suggest a large USD base has formed, turning the core trend higher.

insights.claim: The dollar's November 2026 rally was driven by hawkish Fed commentary, a stronger-than-expected 0.4% m/m US CPI print versus 0.3% expected, and resilient US growth and equities reflecting rotation rather than outflows.
insights.speaker: World Gold Council
insights.so_what: Equity rotation without outflows keeps foreign capital in USD assets, reinforcing dollar strength.

insights.claim: Fed Governor Christopher Waller raised the prospect of a 50bp rate hike in December 2026, alongside elevated CPI and PPI prints that lifted expectations of a December hike.
insights.speaker: World Gold Council
insights.so_what: A 50bp hike is now a live tail; front-end rates and USD are most sensitive to the next Fed communications.

insights.claim: A rising US dollar combined with 10-year TIPS real yields up about 30bp in November 2026 presents a possible 'double whammy' headwind for gold for the foreseeable future.
insights.speaker: World Gold Council
insights.so_what: Notable that the gold industry body itself flags downside; reduce tactical gold exposure while USD holds its breakout and real yields climb.
insights.quote: this presents a possible “double whammy” headwind for gold for the foreseeable future

insights.claim: Leadership turmoil at Nvidia dominated markets in the week to 16 November 2026 and drove volatility across global AI stocks.
insights.speaker: World Gold Council
insights.so_what: Single-company governance shocks at Nvidia now transmit into global AI equity volatility.

insights.claim: In the week to 16 November 2026, Eurozone and UK growth strengthened, China extended its trade truce with the US with stronger exports and mixed inflation, and India saw higher inflation and a wider trade deficit.
insights.speaker: World Gold Council
insights.so_what: Firmer Europe growth and China's trade truce reduce global-recession tail risk; India's widening deficit is a rupee pressure point.

insights.claim: Major global equity markets ended the week to 16 November 2026 higher while bond yields and the US dollar rose and oil prices eased, and US housing weakened despite resilient labour markets.
insights.speaker: World Gold Council
insights.so_what: Equities shrugging off higher yields and a stronger dollar suggests rotation-driven resilience; housing is the rate-sensitive weak link.
